smt-2013-advanced-03.title: Difference of two uniform variables
smt-2013-advanced-03.body:
Let him fall asleep at $4+u$ and wake at $11+v$ (hours), with $u,v$ independent and uniform on $[0,2]$. His sleep is $7+v-u$ hours, so we need $-1\le v-u\le 0$.

- $P(v-u\le 0)=\frac12$ by symmetry.
- $P(v-u<-1)$ is the area of the triangle $\{u-v>1\}$ in the $2\times 2$ square, which has legs $1$ and area $\frac12$, so the probability is $\frac{1/2}{4}=\frac18$.

Therefore the probability is $\frac12-\frac18=\frac38$.

**Answer: $\frac38$**

smt-2013-advanced-03.title: Area of a strip
smt-2013-advanced-03.body:
Plot sleep-in time $s\in[4,6]$ against wake-up time $w\in[11,13]$: a square of area $4$. We want $s+6\le w\le s+7$. The line $w=s+7$ is the diagonal from $(4,11)$ to $(6,13)$; the part of the square on or below it has area $2$. The line $w=s+6$ meets the square from $(5,11)$ to $(6,12)$ and cuts off a corner triangle of area $\frac12$ below it, which must be removed. The strip has area $2-\frac12=\frac32$, so the probability is $\frac{3/2}{4}=\frac38$.

**Answer: $\frac38$**
